item.title: The Hammer Broken: Jeremiah 50, Song of Songs 4, John 6, 1 Peter 3
item.description:
John 6:16-24, 1 Peter 3:1-7, Song of Songs 4:1-7, Jeremiah 50
Jeremiah writes Babylon's funeral song while Babylon is still the hammer of the whole earth: the instrument God judges, the sin searched for and not found, and the strong Redeemer who gives rest to the earth. Plus the groom's praise in Song of Songs 4, 'It is I; do not be afraid' on the Sea of Galilee, and Peter's word to wives and husbands. item.title: Let Your Widows Trust in Me: Jeremiah 49, Song of Songs 3, John 6, 1 Peter 2
item.description:
John 6:1-15, 1 Peter 2:18-25, Song of Songs 3, Jeremiah 49
Jeremiah's oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam, and the puzzling promise to Edom's widows: 'let your widows trust in me.' Also the bride's night search and Solomon's wedding procession in Song of Songs 3, the feeding of the five thousand and the crown Jesus refused in John 6, and the copybook of Christ's suffering in 1 Peter 2. item.title: Settled on His Dregs: Jeremiah 47-48, Song of Songs 2, John 5, 1 Peter 2
item.description:
John 5:31-47, 1 Peter 2:9-17, Song of Songs 2, Jeremiah 47-48
Jeremiah turns to Philistia and Moab: the sword of the Lord that cannot be quiet, Moab settled on its dregs and never poured from vessel to vessel, and a surprising promise at the end. Plus the little foxes of Song of Songs 2, the witnesses of John 5, and Peter's sojourners and exiles. item.title: Whose Word Will Stand: Jeremiah 44-46, Song of Songs 1, John 5, 1 Peter 2
item.description:
John 5:16-30, 1 Peter 2:1-8, Song of Songs 1, Jeremiah 44-46
Jeremiah's last sermon meets an open refusal in Egypt, God answers with 'whose word will stand, mine or theirs?', and Baruch is told not to seek great things for himself. The Song of Songs begins, Jesus claims the Father's work and the Father's honor in John 5, and Peter calls newborn believers to crave the word and come to the Living Stone. item.title: Packed for Egypt: Jeremiah 39-43, Ecclesiastes 12, John 5, 1 Peter 1
item.description:
John 5:1-15, 1 Peter 1:17-25, Ecclesiastes 12, Jeremiah 39-43
Jerusalem falls, Zedekiah is blinded, and an Ethiopian who trusted God walks out alive. Then the survivors swear to obey whatever God says, wait ten days for the answer, and go to Egypt anyway. Also: the end of Ecclesiastes, the man at the pool of Bethesda, and the imperishable word in 1 Peter. item.title: Torn Scroll, Untorn Robes: Jeremiah 35-38, Ecclesiastes 11, John 4, 1 Peter 1
item.description:
John 4:43-54, 1 Peter 1:10-16, Ecclesiastes 11, Jeremiah 35-38
Jehoiakim cut Jeremiah's scroll column by column and burned it, yet no one in the room tore his robe. We go deeper into the Rechabites, then follow Jeremiah through the burned scroll, the dungeon, and the muddy cistern, and ask whether he lied to Zedekiah's officials. Also Ecclesiastes 11 on sowing without knowing, the official who believed Jesus' word in John 4, and the prophets who served us in 1 Peter 1.
